title: Slice 0 and Slice 1 work packages
description: Source of truth for the work breakdown. docs/architecture/slice-plan.md renders its tables from this file, and docs/architecture/tools/check_work_packages.py validates it: roles are known, titles read as plain English, dependencies are acyclic, concurrent packages own disjoint paths, every port is referenced consistently, and every package has at least one done criterion that a command or a named test can check. Sizes are relative effort, not a schedule: S=1, M=3, L=5, XL=8.

work_packages.title: Create the Cargo workspace and the architecture checks
work_packages.summary: Create the workspace with the twelve library crates and four binaries from ADR 0002 as empty compiling shells. A shell has no dependencies and only a short crate comment; the package that owns the crate adds its dependencies and its module declarations. Each crate inherits the workspace lints, and the four crates that must stay free of I/O carry their clippy ban list. Every binary prints that it is not implemented and exits with an error. External dependency versions are pinned in the manifest of the crate that uses them, so parallel packages never edit the root manifest. Write the xtask architecture check test-first, including the source-scan rules that the negative-test catalog lists as static checks. This package merges before any other package touches a crate directory.

done.check: The workspace builds from a clean checkout.
The architecture check passes on the skeleton.
Each rule DEP-01 to DEP-04 and DEP-08 to DEP-10 has a failing fixture that makes the check exit non-zero.

Static checks ST-01 (no safe.directory wildcard), ST-02 (no equality comparison on signatures), ST-03 (no shell spawn), ST-04 (dangerous container flags only in the posture verifier deny list and tests), ST-05 (no merge or deploy path without the approval check) and ST-09 (workspace reads only through the ingestion module) each have a failing fixture.
The clippy bans fire: a scratch crate using each banned call fails under the same clippy.toml.
Lints and formatting are clean.
The set of crates in cargo metadata equals the set in crate-dependency-rules.json, so every listed crate and binary exists as an empty compiling shell.
Every crate sets [lints] workspace = true, and a crate that does not fails the architecture check (DEP-06).

work_packages.title: Define identifiers, value types and contract types in the domain crate
work_packages.summary: Write the pure types: identifiers, tenant scope, versions, hashes, timestamps, fidelity, execution mode, every status enum with the exact serialized names from state-machine.json, and one Rust type per schema. Add the ledger chain hash as a pure function. No I/O, no clock, no randomness.

done.check: Every valid example under schemas/examples deserializes into its type and serializes back to an equal JSON value.
Status enum names equal the state lists in state-machine.json.
The ledger chain hash reproduces values computed by an independent script on a fixture chain.
Clippy bans and the architecture check pass for the crate.
done.command: cargo clippy -p factory-domain -- -D warnings && cargo xtask check-architecture

work_packages.title: Implement the four state machines exactly as the transition tables
work_packages.summary: Write the Job, StageRun, Attempt and TaskNode transition functions as pure code, the named guard predicates, the invalidation rules, and the conformance and property tests that read state-machine.json. This package is test-first by construction: the conformance test is written before the functions.

done.check: For each machine the accepted (from, event) pairs equal the JSON, and every other pair is rejected with a typed error and no state change.
Every guard id in the JSON has a named predicate, and every predicate has an entry.
Ten thousand generated command sequences never leave the tables (QA-1).
The invalidation function reproduces every row of the JSON invalidation table.
Adding a transition to a copy of the JSON makes the conformance test fail, so the test is not vacuous.
The generated tables in state-machine.md are in sync.

work_packages.title: Define the port traits and the labelled fakes with shared contract tests
work_packages.summary: Fix version 1 of the port traits and their closed error enums from the sketches in this plan, and build testkit: faithful in-memory fakes that each report fidelity fake, the scripted adversarial runtime FX-ADV, a controllable clock FX-CLOCK, and generic contract test suites that run against any implementation. The same suites later run against the real adapters, which is how a fake is kept honest.

done.check: Each contract suite passes against its in-memory fake: store (CAS, lease fencing, tenant scope, ledger chain, outbox), artifact store, sandbox, workspace, agent runtime, model broker, change host.
Every fake reports fidelity fake.
The scripted adversarial runtime obeys any script it is given and records every prompt it receives with the structured parts separated (FX-ADV).
ChangeHost has no method whose name starts with merge, and testkit is a dev-dependency only.
Every public trait documents its preconditions, postconditions, closed error set and idempotency.
The architect reviewed the port surface and the revision is tagged ports-v1.

work_packages.title: Validate contracts and load agent, profile, project and policy definitions
work_packages.summary: Embed the schemas, implement OutputValidator with hard size and depth limits, and load agent manifests, domain capability profiles, project manifests and the policy files. The loader follows the parser contract written at the top of policies/security.yaml: typed structs with unknown keys rejected, a single document, no anchors, aliases or merge keys, a schema version that must match, and a policy hash over the canonical form. The existing schema examples and their expectation files are the test oracle.
inputs: policies/ as written by the security specialist

done.check: Every valid example validates and every invalid example is rejected at the path named in its .expect file.
Every keyword used by the schemas (if/then/else, dependentSchemas, contains, oneOf, not) behaves as in check-jsonschema, proven by the same examples.
A YAML parser is chosen from at least two maintained candidates, with serde_yaml excluded as deprecated, and the comparison is written down.
Loaders reject a manifest whose prompt hash does not match the prompt file, and name the file and field in the error.
The policy files in policies/ load without error.
The schema suite still passes.

Policy loading is strict: an unknown key, a wrong schema version, a duplicate key, an anchor, alias or merge key, a wrong type, an invalid regex or glob, and a missing default action each fail the load (NT-POL-03). Policy is read only from the protected configuration source, never from an environment path, a feature branch or the target repository (NT-POL-01).
done.command: cargo nextest run -p factory-contracts negative_nt_pol_01 negative_nt_pol_03 st_06

done.check: Adapter output with an unknown field, wrong types, depth 10,000, a 10 MB body, invalid UTF-8 or a traversal path is rejected before any parse that could exhaust memory (NT-TOOL-09).

work_packages.title: Create the first PostgreSQL migrations and database tests
work_packages.summary: Design and migrate the first schema: tenant, repository, principal, API token with expiry, audience and revocation, webhook delivery with a unique delivery id, job, original request, stage run, attempt with lease columns, task node, artifact metadata, evidence ledger, append-only audit event with actor, policy hash and correlation id, outbox and approval. Encode the rules from ADR 0007 and ADR 0008 in constraints, triggers and roles, and prove them with database tests.

done.check: Migrations run up, redo and up on an empty PostgreSQL, and the committed schema.rs equals diesel print-schema.
An unknown status is rejected for every status column, and the allowed values equal the state lists in state-machine.json.
UPDATE and DELETE on the evidence ledger fail for the application role, and a gapped insert fails.
A foreign key that points at another tenant's row is rejected, and unique constraints include the tenant.
UPDATE of a terminal stage run row fails except for the supersede transition.
The claim, sweep, timeline and ledger-tail queries use index scans on 10,000 generated rows, with plans recorded.
The application role can only INSERT and SELECT on the audit event table: UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE and DROP fail (NT-AUD-01).
A second webhook delivery with the same delivery id violates a unique constraint and is handled without creating a second job or outbox row (supports NT-WH-04).

work_packages.title: Set up continuous integration that runs the same checks as a developer
work_packages.summary: Write one script that runs every check, and a workflow that calls it, so local and CI results cannot drift. A missing tool is reported as BLOCKED with its own exit code. It never counts as a pass. Add the Compose file with PostgreSQL.

done.check: The script runs format, clippy, tests, deny, audit, the architecture check, schema validation, both document checks and the Mermaid check, and exits non-zero on any failure.
With a required tool hidden from PATH the script prints BLOCKED and exits 3, not 0.
Compose brings up a healthy PostgreSQL.
The example environment file holds no secret-looking values.
The workflow runs the same script and is green on the first pull request.
CI actions are pinned to full commit SHAs (ST-10), and a secret scan of the full repository history runs, reporting BLOCKED when the scanner is not installed (ST-08).

work_packages.title: Write the security baseline, policies and supply-chain rules
work_packages.summary: Already in progress with the security specialist. Threat model over the eight trust boundaries, the four policy files, the supply-chain policy, the container profile review for ADR 0003, the set of git hardening options for host git operations, secret redaction rules, and the first prompt-injection corpus.

done.check: The threat model walks all eight trust boundaries with a STRIDE pass and records residual risk.
The four policy files exist: approval, security, quality, model_routing.
Dependency and license policy passes.
The container profile and the host git hardening options are reviewed and written down.
The injection corpus has at least 10 cases covering issue text, repository files and tool output.
The conflicts listed in ADR 0009 are resolved in the policy files: rework cap, automatic approval of allowlisted dependency names, and role resolution by allowlist.

work_packages.title: Initialize tracing and OpenTelemetry for the binaries
work_packages.summary: Provide init functions, the span and attribute naming constants, the conventions page and a local collector configuration. Logs carry the job correlation id.

done.check: Init is idempotent and the span and attribute constants equal the table in the conventions page.
Log lines carry correlation_id when a job span is active.
One span reaches a local OTLP receiver. Without a receiver the test reports BLOCKED.
Every metric, log and trace field name used in code is in the attribute allowlist (ST-07).

work_packages.title: Settle the open Spec Kit questions: revision, checklist, arguments and running in the sandbox
work_packages.summary: Risk-first spike for ADR 0006, narrowed to what the Spec Kit specialist left unverified. Test the proposed revision method, the checklist pre-run and the preset option, the specify skill with clarification markers, an explicit feature directory in the skill arguments, the file-based request input against an adversarial issue body, concurrent runs in separate worktrees, and all four skills inside the hardened sandbox profile. The specialist's host-run recordings stay as labelled evidence. Live runs need an API key and are BLOCKED without one. Protocol-level checks use the labelled fake provider from the agent spike.

done.check: A run manifest records the Spec Kit and host versions, the exact command, exit code, duration and the sha256 of every produced file, for each recorded run.
The report answers each unverified item in ADR 0006 with a pointer to a recorded file, or marks it BLOCKED with the reason.

A recorded revision run follows the proposed method (new feature directory seeded on the host, change by clarify or a reviewed edit) and passes the seven post-conditions. Or the report states the method failed and names the replacement.
The checklist skill produces a checklist without a plan.md through the adapter pre-run, or the failure and the preset attempt are recorded. An empty plan.md is never used.
The file-based request input and the quoted-block fallback are both run against an adversarial issue body. The security specialist accepts one in writing.
The skills start and finish inside the hardened agent profile with a masked .git, or the report names what blocks them.
The verdict is GO, GO with a named fallback, or NO-GO, and ADR 0006 carries the amendment.

work_packages.title: Prove how the agent tools run inside the sandbox behind the broker
work_packages.summary: Risk-first spike for ADR 0005. Install Claude Code and Codex into a hardened container image, start each under the agent profile with a masked .git, point each at a local labelled fake provider through a base URL or settings file with a dummy key, and record the request each sends. Test structured output with the real gate-report schema, the non-interactive permission behavior, cancellation and exit codes. Evaluate the host tool bridge as the hardening target. Real provider calls need an API key and are BLOCKED without one.

done.check: Recordings exist for each tool with version, command, exit code and output, and a manifest checks the required keys.
Each tool is installed into a container image and starts under the hardened profile with a masked .git, or the report names what blocks it.

Each tool is redirected to the labelled fake provider and the request it sends (path, headers, whether the credential came from a file or helper) is recorded, or the report says it cannot be redirected and the fallback in secrets-and-credentials.md section 4.4 is chosen.
The report records whether the structured-output options accept the gate-report schema and what the tool sent.
The report answers every other item in ADR 0005 under 'Not verified' with a pointer to a recording.
The bridge evaluation records GO or NO-GO per tool as the hardening target, with the evidence that the built-in shell was unavailable to the model.
ADR 0005 carries the amendment: accepted version range, bridge verdict and the fallback for any tool that fails.

work_packages.title: Build and pin the sandbox image for the fixture project
work_packages.summary: Build the images the supervisor runs: the agent image (non-root user, the build toolchain and the agent command line tools, no git binary), the verify image (toolchain only), and the egress sidecar image. Pin each by digest and record the digests where the adapter and the gate reports can read them.
inputs: the fixture project decision in this plan

done.check: The build script produces the three images and writes their digests to images.json.
The hardened profile from sandbox-policy.md runs the toolchain offline as a non-root user in the verify image.
No image contains a real credential, a GitHub CLI, a git binary or a secret-looking environment value, and only the agent image contains agent tools.

A suitable base image tag for the pinned Rust toolchain exists, confirmed before the build is written, or the plan records the substitute. Installing each agent tool into the agent image is confirmed or the report names what blocks it.

work_packages.title: Implement the Docker sandbox supervisor and the posture verifier
work_packages.summary: Implement SandboxProvider over the Docker command line as the supervisor in sandbox-policy.md section 9: three network profiles with per-job internal networks and the sidecar, create then inspect then compare against policy then start, the runtime self-check, wall-clock and disk enforcement by the supervisor, redacted log streaming with the daemon log driver off, the janitor, and fail-closed behavior. Gates run in fresh verify containers.

done.check: The sandbox contract suite passes against the Docker adapter as it does against the fake. Without Docker it reports BLOCKED.
The posture verifier rejects each forbidden setting and runs the runtime self-check (NT-SBX-01, NT-SBX-02).
done.command: cargo nextest run -p factory-sandbox negative_nt_sbx_01 negative_nt_sbx_02

done.check: The verify profile has no network, and the agent profile on a per-job internal network reaches no other job, no external address and no metadata address (NT-SBX-03, NT-SBX-04).
done.command: cargo nextest run -p factory-sandbox negative_nt_sbx_03 negative_nt_sbx_04

done.check: Read-only root, capability removal, kernel path masking, the resource limits and the supervisor-enforced wall-clock deadline hold (NT-SBX-06, NT-SBX-07, NT-SBX-08). The disk poll kills a writer that exceeds the cap.
done.command: cargo nextest run -p factory-sandbox negative_nt_sbx_06 negative_nt_sbx_07 negative_nt_sbx_08

done.check: No daemon socket is reachable, no real credential is visible, and a stopped daemon, a missing image, a bad policy file or a failed sidecar leaves the job BLOCKED with nothing run (NT-SBX-12, NT-SBX-13, NT-SBX-14).
done.command: cargo nextest run -p factory-sandbox negative_nt_sbx_12 negative_nt_sbx_13 negative_nt_sbx_14

done.check: Images run only by digest. A tag, an unknown digest or an image that is not pre-pulled is refused (NT-SUP-05).
Process arguments and environments recorded by the spawn recorder contain no secret (NT-SEC-09, sandbox part).
No generated argument vector contains a denied flag, over randomly generated specifications, and nothing in the crate starts a shell (ST-03).
The janitor removes labelled containers, networks and sidecars whose attempt is terminal.

work_packages.title: Implement the PostgreSQL store, the evidence ledger and the local artifact store
work_packages.summary: Implement Store and Tx over Diesel with diesel-async, claim and lease operations, outbox writes, the ledger with chain verification, and LocalFsArtifactStore. The shared contract suite from testkit runs against it.

done.check: The store contract suite passes against PgStore on PostgreSQL in Docker, the same suite that passes against the in-memory fake.
Two concurrent claimers on one ready row produce exactly one winner.
A zombie worker's write with an old lease epoch is rejected.
A fault injected after the outbox insert rolls back the status change, the ledger entry and the outbox row together.
Every repository method refuses to return or change another tenant's rows.
Concurrent appends to one job give a continuous, verifiable chain, and flipping one byte makes the verifier fail.
The artifact store is idempotent, verifies hashes on read, detects a corrupted blob and writes read-only files.
Lease expiry is judged by the database clock, shown with a skewed Clock.
100 interleavings of two workers claiming one job produce exactly one winner, and a renewal with a wrong owner or tenant is refused (NT-LSE-02).
The application role cannot UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE or DROP the audit tables (NT-AUD-01), and the audit events carry actor, policy hash and correlation id.

work_packages.title: Build the durable workflow engine
work_packages.summary: Build admission, the claim loop, leases with heartbeats and the sweeper, attempt result handling with output validation, retry with back-off, the gate framework, rework routing, supersession, human decisions, bounds, the ledger and outbox writes, the StageHandler trait and registry, the job audit verifier, and the production-mode refusal of fake adapters. All of it runs first against the in-memory fakes. The skeleton pre-declares the module lines for every stage and gate directory, so the stage packages add code without editing the files this package owns. It also owns the audit event stream with actor, policy hash and correlation id, and the credential and budget hooks around each attempt (job token issue and revoke through ModelBroker).

done.check: The engine scenario suite, written generically over Store, passes on the in-memory store with scripted fake stage handlers in test mode.
Each invariant INV-01 to INV-11 has a named test.
A runtime that always fails reaches WAITING_FOR_HUMAN within a bounded number of steps (INV-10).
A rework after documentation supersedes the documentation runs, driven by the JSON invalidation table.
Dropping the engine mid-transaction and starting a new one resumes the job without loss or duplication.
Production mode refuses to start with any fake adapter (INV-08).
The audit verifier detects a broken chain, a fake entry in production, and a PASSED run without evidence.
Store::begin_system is called only inside this crate.
A stale worker that resumes after its lease was taken cannot push, comment, start a sandbox or change state (NT-LSE-01).
Missing, blocked or stale gate evidence refuses promotion (NT-MRG-02), and a repeated failing action ends in WAITING_FOR_HUMAN after the stagnation window (NT-BUD-03).
done.command: cargo nextest run -p factory-workflow negative_nt_mrg_02 negative_nt_bud_03

done.check: Every audit event type the policy requires is emitted with actor, policy hash and correlation id, shown by a scripted scenario per type (NT-AUD-03, engine part).
done.command: cargo nextest run -p factory-workflow --test audit every_required_event_type

work_packages.title: Evaluate approval, tool grant, protected path and budget policy as pure rules
work_packages.summary: Write the pure policy functions the guards need, with deny overrides, as policies/security.yaml specifies: requester allowlist, admission, autonomy level from the repository preflight, risk tier, tool grants as the intersection of manifest, policy and stage need, command classes, path normalization and protected-path matching, required approval role, override permission, new-dependency decisions, rework caps and budget checks. When the tests pass, flip policy.status in the policy file to enforced (its owner makes that edit).

done.check: Table-driven tests built from the policy files cover admission, the requester allowlist, tool grants, protected paths, approval roles, overrides and budgets.
A project policy can only tighten: adding an egress host, removing a protected group, raising a limit, enabling level L3 or adding a tool grant is refused; lowering a budget is allowed (NT-POL-02).
Deny overrides allow, and the exception flow works only through the recorded human decision (NT-POL-04).

The forbidden command classes, the never-grantable tools and self-grant attempts are refused, and path normalization defeats traversal, encoding and case tricks (NT-TOOL-02, NT-TOOL-03, NT-TOOL-04, NT-TOOL-05, NT-GATE-04).
done.command: cargo nextest run -p factory-domain negative_nt_tool_02 negative_nt_tool_03 negative_nt_tool_04 negative_nt_tool_05

done.check: A granted tool set never exceeds the manifest's allowed tools, over generated inputs, and an unknown tool or path class is denied.
An override of a mandatory gate of an active profile is refused (INV-07), and a new direct dependency always needs a human (ADR 0009).
The rework cap in the policy file is at most two. A larger value fails the test (ADR 0009).

work_packages.title: Implement the Claude Code and Codex adapters that run inside the sandbox
work_packages.summary: Implement AgentRuntime for both tools following ADR 0005 and the spike verdict: the probe, argument builders from a closed allow list, starting the tool inside the sandbox through the session with the job token and the broker address, output parsing and usage accounting, failure mapping, and cancellation. Live smoke tests need an API key and are BLOCKED without one.

done.check: The probe turns recorded help text into the expected flag observations, and an unsupported version blocks the stage.

Bypass flags are emitted only for a sandbox target whose posture check passed. For any other target the builder refuses. Only allow-listed flags appear, and the flag set differs per stage (the slash-command disable flag is absent for the specification stage).

Repository-resident agent configuration (hooks, environment blocks, MCP servers, instruction files) is never honored: the hostile fixture produces no marker file and no unexpected connection (NT-INJ-07).
The environment of the spawned tool is fixed by the supervisor, and an env parameter or an LD_PRELOAD-style value from the agent has no effect (NT-TOOL-06).
A command that floods output, a command that sleeps past its timeout and background children started with setsid are bounded and the whole process group ends (NT-TOOL-07).
Recorded real outputs parse into outcomes with usage, and malformed output maps to a typed error.
Provider outage, rate limit and missing credential map to the closed error set, using a scripted stand-in process labelled fake.
A live smoke test through the broker records fidelity-real evidence. Without an API key or a binary it reports BLOCKED. A subscription login does not count.
done.command: FACTORY_LIVE=1 cargo nextest run -p factory-runtime --test live_smoke

work_packages.title: Implement the GitHub App adapter for issues, narrowed tokens, draft pull requests and webhooks
work_packages.summary: Implement IssueSource and ChangeHost as a GitHub App: sign the App JWT, mint one installation token per job narrowed to one repository and to the permissions of one stage, revoke it at job end, verify webhook signatures on the raw body, deduplicate deliveries, run the repository protection preflight, push only to factory branches, and write only sanitized text. Merging is not implemented. Requester authorization is the named allowlist from policy, not a GitHub role.
inputs: GitHub REST documentation read at implementation time

done.check: Webhook signature verification passes known-answer vectors computed by an independent script, rejects missing, malformed, SHA-1-only and tampered signatures, uses the raw body and compares in constant time (NT-WH-02, NT-WH-03, ST-02).
done.command: cargo nextest run -p factory-github negative_nt_wh_02 negative_nt_wh_03

done.check: Webhook state is re-fetched from the API, not trusted from the payload, events arriving out of order are handled, and the factory ignores its own events and other bots' (NT-WH-06, NT-WH-09).
done.command: cargo nextest run -p factory-github negative_nt_wh_06 negative_nt_wh_09

done.check: A token is minted for one repository only and carries only the permissions of the stage, and access to another repository fails (NT-AUTHZ-06, NT-AUTHZ-07).
done.command: cargo nextest run -p factory-github negative_nt_authz_06 negative_nt_authz_07

done.check: An App that holds a forbidden permission is refused at onboarding, or capped at level L0 (NT-AUTHZ-09). A repository without branch protection, without checks pinned to the App, or with the App in a bypass list runs at level L0 (NT-MRG-07).
done.command: cargo nextest run -p factory-github negative_nt_authz_09 negative_nt_mrg_07

done.check: Text bound for GitHub is blocked when it holds a secret, and markdown with image, link and reference tricks cannot carry data out (NT-SEC-03, NT-SEC-04).
done.command: cargo nextest run -p factory-github negative_nt_sec_03 negative_nt_sec_04

done.check: Tokens are revoked at the end of a job that succeeded, failed, was cancelled and was orphaned (NT-SEC-10, GitHub part).
The factory's own process arguments and environments hold no token (NT-SEC-09, GitHub part).
Opening a draft pull request is idempotent for the same head branch, and the contract suite passes as it does for the fake.
No merge call exists in the crate, and rate-limit responses are handled with back-off.
A live smoke test opens and closes a draft pull request on the fixture repository using a registered App. Without the App credentials it reports BLOCKED.
done.command: FACTORY_LIVE=1 cargo nextest run -p factory-github --test live_smoke

work_packages.title: Write the agent manifests, prompts and the general-software profile
work_packages.summary: Write the manifest and versioned prompt for each Slice 1 role: intake classifier, specification writer, specification reviewer, architect, planner, builder, code reviewer, documentation writer, documentation reviewer. Write the general-software profile. Placements are sandbox only. Add per-agent conformance fixtures. These are conformance checks, not quality evaluations.

done.check: Every manifest and profile in the repository validates through the loader, and every prompt hash matches its file.
Every manifest allows only the sandbox placement in Slice 1, and writers and readers are consistent with their tool access.
Rendered prompts keep untrusted inputs inside the delimited data section, shown by a deterministic string test per agent.
Each agent has conformance fixtures, and the scripted fake runtime's outputs validate against the agent's output schema.

work_packages.title: Write the documentation policy and the readability rubric with a test corpus
work_packages.summary: Define the rules the Human-Readable Artifact Quality Gate checks, the minimal documentation set per change type with the Diataxis mapping, and a corpus of good and bad examples, including every bad example from the master prompt and Portuguese samples.
inputs: master prompt: communication policy and section 10

done.check: The corpus has at least 8 good and 20 bad examples, and each bad example declares the rule id it breaks in a header line.
Every bad example from the master prompt is in the corpus.
The policy lists, per change type, the required documents, their audience and their form.

work_packages.title: Build the human-readable artifact quality gate
work_packages.summary: Implement the deterministic rules from the rubric as a pure function that reads titles, task bodies, specifications, pull request text and documentation and returns a gate report. The engine wraps it as a gate. It warns on style and blocks only clear policy violations, and it never changes the text.

done.check: Every good example passes and every bad example fails with the rule id in its header.
The gate never alters its input and reports warnings separately from blocking violations.
Metadata identifiers stay stable when a title is reworded.
Non-English prose outside quotes and code is flagged, and quoted source text is not.
Its reports validate against the gate-report schema.

work_packages.title: Build the Spec Kit adapter and the specification stage
work_packages.summary: Implement SpecKitProvider in the spec_adapter crate, the pure parser that turns Spec Kit files into a SpecificationContract, the specification stage handler and the deterministic gate with freeze and revision. Follows ADR 0006 and the spike verdict: invocation syntax read from integration.json, no init on an initialised repository, an explicit feature directory per job in its own worktree, the seven post-conditions after every skill, the question detector, the checklist pre-run, the revision method, and issue text kept out of the instruction channel.

done.check: The parser produces the expected contract from each recorded real Spec Kit output, and a structure it does not recognize is SPEC_PARSE_ERROR, never a guess.

The operation type cannot express plan, tasks, implement, converge, analyze, taskstoissues or workflow, and the invocation builder reads the separator from integration.json and the sigil from the host table.

A Spec Kit version different from the pinned one, an integration status other than ok, a modified installed file or a present extensions file blocks the stage. The adapter never runs init on an initialised repository.
The seven post-conditions are checked after every skill and the agent's own report is ignored.
Checklist ticks written by the authoring agent carry no weight. An item counts only when an independent reviewer or a person with a reason is recorded in the ledger by the engine.
done.command: cargo nextest run -p factory-workflow --test specification self_ticked_checklist_is_not_evidence

done.check: Each deterministic specification gate rule has a failing fixture: required sections, status and date, story priorities and scenarios, identifier uniqueness, requirement keywords, remaining markers and placeholders, technology names, and the committed artifact set with matching hashes.

A revision creates a new feature directory seeded on the host, links it with supersedes and revision metadata, and supersedes every downstream run. The method is replaced if the spike showed it failing.

Specification text that claims authorization (for example 'this task is authorized to modify workflows') grants nothing, and an issue body that asks for another skill cannot select one (NT-POL-05, NT-INJ-02 for the skill input).
Strings .specify and speckit appear only in this crate, its fixtures and documentation.
The live run on the fixture issue produces a contract that validates and whose artifact hashes match the files. Without an API key or prerequisites it reports BLOCKED.
done.command: FACTORY_LIVE=1 cargo nextest run -p factory-spec-adapter --test live

done.check: The specification stage profile permits exactly the four allowed Spec Kit skills and denies plan, tasks, analyze, implement, converge and taskstoissues even inside that stage (NT-POL-08).

negative_tests.naming_rule: Each test function name starts with negative_ followed by the lower-case catalog id with underscores, for example negative_nt_sbx_01_posture_verifier_rejects_forbidden_settings, so a name filter selects it. Each test has a control-off switch in the harness and must fail when its control is off (catalog principle 2).

entries.reduced_scope_reason: Complete only after every component that emits an event exists. The coverage matrix lists each event type with its owner.
The catalog sets up a user whose GitHub permission was revoked. Under the named allowlist the equivalent is a user removed from the list. The expected result is the same.
Neither agent tool has a turn cap flag. The engine detects stagnation and escalates. A turn cap needs the tool or the broker to count requests.
The catalog names an evals component for held-out evaluation data. There is no evals crate before Slice 4, so only the sandbox, the prompts and the sinks are tested.

The catalog assumes factory-mediated tool calls (exec.shell, approval.grant). With the agent inside the sandbox its own tools are contained by the container, not parsed by the factory. The test asserts that no factory-level effect or grant is reachable from the agent.
The sink collector includes NATS messages and memory stores. Neither exists before Slice 2 and Slice 4.
Covers commands the supervisor runs (gates, dependency fetch, ingestion). The agent's own in-container shell is covered by NT-SBX-* instead.
Path policy is tested on the pure function and on ingestion. The agent's in-container file tools are contained by the sandbox.
Argument injection is tested on the command classifier used by supervisor-run commands. The agent's own commands are contained by the sandbox.
Tests the environment the supervisor gives the tool and the commands it runs. The agent's own env parameter does not exist as a factory tool.
The catalog names an events component. Slice 1 has the outbox row and the unique delivery id. Publishing to NATS and the idempotent consumer are Slice 2.

gaps.uncovered: Publishing to NATS and the idempotent event consumer
gaps.reason: The events crate is deferred to Slice 2. Slice 1 stores the outbox row and the unique delivery id.

gaps.uncovered: Held-out evaluation data in the evals component
gaps.reason: There is no evals crate before Slice 4. Sandbox, prompts and sinks are covered.

gaps.uncovered: NATS messages and memory stores as sinks in the canary sweep
A turn cap on the agent tool
gaps.reason: Claude Code 2.1.311 has no --max-turns flag and Codex exec shows no budget flag. Only stagnation detection and the broker ceiling bound the run.
gaps.resolves_in: needs a decision: broker request counting, or a tool that supports a cap

gaps.uncovered: Factory-mediated tool calls by the agent (exec.run, fs.read, fs.write, exec.shell, approval.grant)
gaps.reason: With the agent tool inside the sandbox its own tools are not mediated by the factory. The container, the broker and the ingestion pipeline contain it instead. The catalog's setups assume mediation (the host tool bridge).
gaps.resolves_in: If a human chooses the host tool bridge, these tests apply in full to the bridge tools

gaps.uncovered: Event types whose emitting component is built late
gaps.reason: The coverage test can only finish when every emitter exists.
gaps.resolves_in: end of Slice 1, by the coverage matrix
